schema_note: Matches the section layout used by dorm_fridge.json, chest_freezer.json, kitchen_fridge.json. IMPORTANT: unlike those three, NO value in the electrical section has been measured yet. Every electrical number here is nameplate or derived. Treat as a pre-measurement hypothesis file.

identity.description: Carrier Infinity ICS gas furnace, condensing, variable-speed ECM blower, three-stage gas valve
identity.model_plug: PL4 model plug = HK70EZ018 (3.5T080 row of the cabinet-door PL4 MODEL PLUG CHART). Pin resistances measured 10.88 kohm (pins 1-4, spec 11) and 17.70 kohm (pins 2-3, spec 18) => MATCH (pins 2-3 encode size: 11/18/24/33/39 = 060/3.5T080/5T080/100/120). Confirms the unit is configured 3.5-ton / 80,000 BTU. Cooling airflow for the 3.5-ton config = 1225 CFM at 350 CFM/ton (the door 'A/C OR CF AIRFLOW SELECTION CHART' basis) OR 1400 CFM at 400 CFM/ton, selectable via SW1-5 (Carrier product data 58MVC-5PD p.9-10; SW1-5 position not yet read) - both legitimate, see estimated_running_draw_by_stage.derivation_note. Door chart also gives default A/C airflow 1050 CFM and default continuous-fan 525 CFM (switches OFF). Verified by Ron 2026-08-07.
identity.nameplate_text_as_read: INFINITY ICS MODEL 58MVC DELUXE 4-WAY MULTIPOISE VARIABLE-SPEED MULTI-STAGE CONDENSING GAS FURNACE Series 100, Input Rates: 60,000 thru 120,000 Btuh / 58MVC080-F-10114
identity.control_system: Carrier Infinity ICS, COMMUNICATING (CONFIRMED 2026-08-07). Thermostat = Carrier Infinity Touch SYSTXCCITC01-B (fw v2.00), communicating-only, over the 4-wire ABCD bus. Pinout (corroborated by the infinitive project + HVAC-Talk, and matches the original 38400 8N1 note): A/B = RS-485 data pair at 38400 8N1 (A=green Data A, B=yellow Data B); C/D = 24VAC (C=white Com, D=red Hot). Tap A/B ONLY - never connect to C/D (24VAC). Stage/status readable via infinitive-style decode - see control_board_label.resolved. PLAN: read bus via a genuine FTDI USB-RS485-WE-1800-BT cable on a Linux box; firmware-v2.00 may need an infinitive fork (infinitive-modern / hass-infinitive) - TBD before 2026-08-17.
identity.thermostat_model: Carrier Infinity Touch SYSTXCCITC01-B, firmware v2.00

channel_binding.binding_note: NOT YET BOUND. The furnace differs from the other three loads: it is hardwired to a dedicated 15 A branch circuit, not cord-and-plug. Powering it from the inverter requires either a cord-and-plug conversion at the furnace junction box or a panel interlock. Do not backfeed a receptacle.

nameplate_limits.source: product data 58MVC-5PD electrical table, unit size 080-14
nameplate_limits.interpretation_note: maximum_unit_amps and blower FLA are ceilings for the module at max airflow and max static. They are NOT expected running values. Do not size the inverter budget from them.

blower_motor_nameplate.as_read: GE ECM Motors 3.0 / GC08 / by Regal-Beloit / 1/2 HP / 120/240 V / mfd 9/18/2009 / 19 0041BX
blower_motor_nameplate.read_location: motor nameplate, best viewed from the filter box with the filter removed
blower_motor_nameplate.note: Physical-label read RESOLVES the earlier aftermarket-catalog ambiguity: genuine ECM 3.0 (not the 2.3/2.5 some replacement listings imply). Confirms a brushless-DC, torque/airflow-controlled soft-ramp motor => NO locked-rotor inrush (consistent with the transients section); only the ~1 ms ECM DC-bus charge inrush at 115 V power-up applies. Carrier orderable assembly for the 58MVC blower is 58MV660006 (aftermarket cross-ref, medium confidence, NOT confirmed vs the factory parts diagram; reportedly a 2.5-gen substitute). Full GE model/serial and the 5SME39 module number were not transcribed.

control_board_label.series_note: HK42FZ035 is the OEM control board for this furnace. HK42FZ0354011 is the full board marking (035 base + 4011 version); H84272835A81 is a secondary/OEM marking on the same board.
control_board_label.compatibility_confirmed: RepairClinic PartDetail 2347709: 'Genuine OEM Part # HK42FZ035' and 'This part fits your Carrier Furnace 58MVC080-F-10114' (green check). Confirmed via Ron's screenshot 2026-08-07.
control_board_label.resolved: COMMUNICATING (2026-08-07). Installed thermostat = Carrier Infinity Touch SYSTXCCITC01-B (v2.00), a communicating-only control => the ABCD bus IS present; HK42FZ035 pairs with the Infinity control over it. Earlier suspicion that HK42FZ035 = non-communicating was WRONG. Consequence: the furnace's actual stage (low/med/high), commanded blower CFM, and status may be readable directly off the ABCD bus (community reverse-engineering exists, e.g. the 'infinitive'/'Infinitude' projects) - a cleaner stage-state source than inferring stage from the current clamp. Worth evaluating for the measurement plan.
control_board_label.source: control board read by Ron + RepairClinic PartDetail 2347709 (screenshot) 2026-08-07

estimated_running_draw_by_stage.derivation_note: ECM shaft power scales approximately as CFM^3 against a fixed duct system curve. Anchored at an assumed ~500 W near the blower's max airflow. Airflows VERIFIED against Carrier product data 58MVC-5PD p.9-10 (unit size 080-14), 2026-08-07: HEATING airflow Low=540, Medium=695, High=1220 CFM - with SW1-3 (low/med rise-adjust) and SW1-4 (comfort/eff) OFF; SW1-3 ON raises Low->620, Medium->800. COOLING airflow for a 3.5-ton coil = 1225 CFM at 350 CFM/ton OR 1400 CFM at 400 CFM/ton, selectable via SW1-5 (position not yet read); the blower 'Maximum' row = 1400 CFM (1375 at the certified 0.5 ESP). So 1225 and 1400 are BOTH legitimate cooling figures (SW1-5-dependent) - an earlier note that called 1400 a mistake was itself wrong. The CFM values are certified/confirmed; the est W/amps below remain UNVERIFIED cube-law estimates. Inducer (also variable-speed ECM) and control board estimated separately and added.

stages.source: derived from certified airflow, cube law

estimated_running_draw_by_stage.standby_note: ECM module quiescent draw plus control board. Continuous, 24/7. At 12 W this is ~0.29 kWh/day of inverter load even with zero heat calls. Non-trivial against the LEAF energy budget - verify by measurement.

transients.lra_note: THIS LOAD HAS NO LOCKED-ROTOR INRUSH. Both the blower and the inducer are ECM (electronically commutated) and ramp under microprocessor control over several seconds. This is a categorical difference from the chest freezer's PTC-start induction compressor. In this respect the furnace behaves like the kitchen fridge's BLDC inverter compressor, not like the chest freezer.

events.repeat: once per heat call, all stages
events.detail: Carrier silicon-nitride hot surface igniter runs at line voltage with no external regulator. Cold element resistance is low, so expect a higher inrush spike in roughly the first second before it settles. Blower is OFF during this window (blower-ON delay); inducer is running at pre-purge speed.
events.source: estimated from typical SiN igniter power and the 58MVC ignition sequence

events.repeat: ONLY at 115 V power-up (breaker or disconnect), NOT per heat cycle
events.detail: The ECM module stays energized between cycles; speed is commanded via 24 V PWM inputs, not by switching line power. So this inrush does not recur per cycle. It DOES occur every time a load-shedding relay restores power to the furnace - an argument for not relay-switching this load.

power_factor.note: UNKNOWN AND IMPORTANT. The inverter is VA-limited, not W-limited. ECM drives without active PFC can run PF 0.5-0.6, which would nearly double the apparent power versus the watt figures above. The igniter is resistive (PF ~1.0). Measure W and VA separately for every stage.

control_constants.overcurrent_trip_rationale: Set for low-heat-locked operation (est. 0.8 A steady, 2.4 A igniter transient). Provides margin over the igniter without masking a fault. If SW1-2 low-heat lock is NOT engaged, raise to 6.0 A to clear the estimated 4.0 A high-fire draw. Re-derive after measurement.
control_constants.overcurrent_hold_rationale: Must exceed the 17 s igniter warm-up or the latch will fire on every normal ignition. Compare: the kitchen fridge latch fired on a legitimate 1.9 A defrost step held >20 s.
control_constants.min_run_rationale: Do not interrupt a heat call. Unlike the compressors there is no hot-restart damage hazard (the gas valve simply closes), but a power interruption aborts and restarts the entire ignition sequence, wasting a full igniter warm-up cycle, and repeated attempts will drive the control to a 3-try lockout.
control_constants.post_power_reset_behavior: First cycle after any power reset is forced to 16 minutes of low heat before the control will consider stepping up, unless the thermostat is satisfied first. Convenient in a backup-power scenario, but do not rely on it by deliberately power-cycling.
control_constants.blower_off_delay_note: Selectable at the control board. The blower continues after burner shutoff to extract residual heat - this tail is part of the electrical load and must not be cut short by load shedding.
control_constants.stage_lock_switch: Board has FOUR DIP banks, verified against the board's own function legend (cabinet-door schematic) + board photos (Ron 2026-08-07): SW1 (8-pos SETUP), SW2 (3-pos 'AC' cooling airflow), SW3 (3-pos 'CF' continuous-fan airflow), SW4 (3-pos). SW2/SW3 select airflow via the door 'A/C OR CF AIRFLOW SELECTION CHART' (350 CFM/ton) and do NOT stage heat. Heat staging IS switch-selectable: SW1-2 = Low-Heat Only (force low fire), SW4-2 = Med-heat (force medium) - so the original 'SW1-2 low / SW4-2 med' literature was RIGHT; an earlier note here that claimed 'no SW4' was wrong (SW4 is a fourth bank that was just off-frame in the first photo). SW1 legend: 1=Status Code Recall, 2=Low-Heat Only, 3=Low-Heat Rise Adj, 4=Comfort/Efficiency Adj, 5=Cooling CFM/Ton, 6=Component Test, 7&8=Blower Off-Delay. SW4 legend: 1=Twinning Main(OFF)/Sec(ON), 2=Med-heat, 3=Future Use. AS-FOUND 2026-08-07: SW4 all OFF (Main unit, med-heat NOT forced, future unused); SW1-2 as-found state NOT yet read. NOTE: the ON orientation is printed on the switch bodies (the schematic legend does not show it) - see as-found board photos in the repo. OPEN: whether the SW1-2 / SW4-2 manual overrides take effect under the communicating Infinity control (they are furnace-board 'Manual Switch' overrides so they likely do, but unconfirmed).
control_constants.recommended_backup_mode: SW1-2 low-heat-only. See thermal section: low fire alone covers the measured design load, so this costs nothing in capacity while cutting estimated draw from ~426 W to ~79 W.
control_constants.load_shed_policy: DO NOT SHED THE FURNACE. Shed the fridge and freezer instead and let the furnace run to completion. Rationale: (a) restoring furnace power re-triggers the ECM DC bus inrush, (b) an aborted cycle wastes a 17 s igniter warm-up, (c) repeated aborts risk lockout.
control_constants.source: Carrier product data + troubleshooting literature; trip thresholds are proposals pending measurement

house_ua_out_btuh_per_f.note: Output-side envelope conductance, from regression of 2022-23 daily gas against local monthly climate normals. (The earlier 'warm-winter bias' caveat on 2022-23 is WITHDRAWN: five-season duty analysis shows 2022-23 sits exactly on the 5-season mean duty - it is representative, not warm. See duty_cycle.multi_season_summary.) UA and balance point still await daily outdoor temps to re-fit across all 5 seasons - highest-value open item.
house_ua_out_btuh_per_f.source: regression on utility daily gas export 08/03/2022-09/05/2023

balance_point_f.note: Monthly-resolution fit cannot resolve this well above 63 F. Needs daily local airport-station temperatures to sharpen.

stage_adequacy.note: Low fire output (30,000 Btuh) exceeds design load (20,000-24,000 Btuh). Medium and high fire are almost certainly never required for steady-state heating in this house; they appear only during recovery from the 63 F night setback. Equipment is roughly 3x oversized at high fire.
stage_adequacy.source: derived from UA and stage outputs

duty_cycle.basis: FIVE full heating seasons (2021-22 through 2025-26), DTE daily gas exports, baseload-subtracted, assuming low fire throughout (justified by stage_adequacy above). Recomputed by tools/gas_heating_budget.py from data/gas/*.csv; the 2022-23 detail below is the reference season and doubles as the script's self-test.

multi_season_summary.note: 2022-23 (the season the whole thermal model was built on) lands exactly on the 5-season mean duty (0.26) -> it is REPRESENTATIVE, not the warm-winter outlier earlier assumed. Seasonal average duty is stable across five winters (0.23-0.29); the PEAK, however, has grown - see peak_observed.
multi_season_summary.source: tools/gas_heating_budget.py over data/gas/ (2021-01-02..2026-08-08, 2045 days, 0 gaps, 0 overlap conflicts)

peak_observed.dates: worst single day 2026-02-11, within the 2025-26 season
peak_observed.note: REVISED to the five-season worst (2025-26). The 2022-23 Elliott snap is the MILDEST of the five winters' peaks and is superseded here for worst-case sizing. Recent winters ran the furnace 72-78% over their worst 4 days (2024-25 = 0.72, 2025-26 = 0.78), with single days near 0.89 low-fire duty. CAVEAT: single-day peaks are soft - 51-67% of daily reads are DTE-interpolated (Estimated Read=Yes); 4-day and seasonal figures are robust, single-day peaks indicative only. Daily outdoor temps would re-apportion interpolated intervals by degree-day and sharpen these.

prior_peak_elliott_2022.note: Winter Storm Elliott, the Dec 2022 Arctic outbreak. 4-day interpolated interval average.

gas_baseload_ccf_per_day.note: Non-furnace gas (water heater, range). Winter figure is higher because incoming mains temperature drops. Confirmed consistent across summer 2023 (0.373) and summer 2026 (0.349) exports.

duty_cycle.source: DTE daily gas exports (data/gas/, 5 full seasons) via tools/gas_heating_budget.py; electrical duty inferred from gas, not measured

estimated_electrical_energy.december_breakdown: 9.8 h at ~79 W running + 14.2 h at ~12 W standby
estimated_electrical_energy.note: Low-heat-locked. Compare against fridge (~1.3 kWh/day) and chest freezer (~1.2 kWh/day): the furnace is the SMALLEST of the three electrical loads, despite being the largest thermal load in the house.
estimated_electrical_energy.source: estimated stage draw x measured gas-derived duty cycle

inverter_compatibility.waveform_requirement: PURE SINE WAVE REQUIRED. ECM blower, ECM inducer, and a microprocessor control board. Modified sine will at best run the ECM hot and noisy.
inverter_compatibility.neutral_ground_note: CRITICAL AND OFTEN MISSED. The furnace proves flame by rectifying a microamp AC current through the flame to chassis ground. This requires correct line/neutral polarity AND a neutral-to-ground bond. Many portable inverters have a floating output. Failure signature: burner lights, runs 5-7 s, drops out, retries, locks out after 3-4 attempts. Looks like a gas or flame-sensor fault; is actually an electrical bonding fault. Verify the inverter's bond before diagnosing anything else.

cross_load_notes.surge_ranking: Of the three loads, ONLY the chest freezer has a true locked-rotor inrush (PTC-start induction compressor). The kitchen fridge (BLDC inverter compressor, measured 1.5 A peak) and the furnace (ECM blower and inducer) both soft-start. The 1 kW inverter's surge exposure is therefore dominated by a single load.
cross_load_notes.steady_state_worst_case_detail: furnace low fire 0.8 A + fridge defrost 1.9 A + freezer running ~1.5 A = ~4.2 A, roughly 480 W. Comfortably under 1 kW. The three loads do NOT need to time-share on average power.
cross_load_notes.revised_hypothesis: The original 'each load gets the inverter 1/3 of the time' framing appears unnecessary. The binding constraint is surge coincidence involving the chest freezer, not aggregate steady draw. A start-interlock that prevents the freezer compressor from starting within a few seconds of any other event may be sufficient to run all three concurrently.
cross_load_notes.kitchen_fridge_defrost_confirmation: The 1.9 A defrost figure confirms the leading hypothesis for the overnight overcurrent latch event (step to ~2.38 A settling to ~1.9 A, held >20 s against a 1.5 A / 20 s trip). That was defrost heater engagement, not a fault.
cross_load_notes.source: user-measured fridge values + estimated furnace values

measurement_plan.method_note: Force heat calls from the thermostat in warm weather. Keep runs short. Use the control board setup switches to isolate stages rather than waiting for the adaptive algorithm to select one.
measurement_plan.sensing_note: Measure at the furnace 115 V feed at the junction box, upstream of everything, so blower + inducer + igniter + control board land in one signal. The blower access panel has an interlock switch that kills 115 V when opened - plan the tap accordingly. Do NOT use a 100 A CT: at 0.8 A that is 0.8 percent of full scale. Use a 5-10 A split-core, or pass the hot conductor through a larger CT 5 times for 5x sensitivity.

provenance.furnace_electrical_values: NONE MEASURED. Nameplate values from Carrier product data catalog 58MVC-5PD (Edition 09/10). Per-stage running estimates derived from certified airflow tables via ECM cube-law scaling - low confidence, superseded on first measurement.
provenance.duty_cycle_values: Derived from DTE daily gas usage exports now committed under data/gas/ (2021-01-02..2026-08-08, 2045 days, 0 gaps, 5 full heating seasons) via tools/gas_heating_budget.py. Method: baseload subtraction then division by stage input rate. Originally single-season (2022-23); expanded to 5 seasons 2026-08-10, which confirmed the duty (mean 0.26) and revised the peak upward (see duty_cycle).
provenance.thermal_values: Regression of monthly gas against 1991-2020 local climate normals. Daily local airport-station observations were not available; substituting them is the highest-value open item for tightening UA and balance point.
